body_md: Estimate \eqref{pro2} gives $\langle t\rangle^{-3/2}$ decay for the first derivative of the stream-function profile, improving the $\langle t\rangle^{-6/5}$ rate in \cite[Theorem~1.2]{CJWZ25}. The present statement uses $H_k^4$ data, whereas \cite[Theorem~1.2]{CJWZ25} uses $H_k^3$ data so they are not directly comparable. The loss of $|k|^\theta$, for arbitrarily small $\theta>0$, comes from bounding the logarithmic correction in the inner solution $\Phi_\epsilon^\iota$ by an algebraic loss; see \eqref{log:loss} and the following discussion in Section~\ref{Inner}. The further loss of $|k|^{1/2}$ relative to dimensional scaling arises from the factor $|k\delta(\Lambda)|^{1/2}$ in the preliminary pointwise bound \eqref{prelim:pointwise} at the start of Section \ref{sec:main:results}. The other principal time-decay and quadratic-depletion rates agree with the Kolmogorov result and are obtained here for the shears under Assumption~\ref{MaAs}.

title: Remark
body_md: We comment on the design of the norm in the $S_{\delta(\Lambda)}^j$ region. This region contains the critical layers which logarithmically fail to be bounded and are thus incompatible with the $L^\infty$ type norms used away from the critical layers. To capture the pointwise vanishing the $H^1$ norm is appropriately weighted by $\delta^{-1/2}(\Lambda)$ to ensure $L^\infty$ control by $(\delta(\Lambda))^{-\sigma_1- \sigma_2}.$ However, when $|k \delta(\Lambda)| \gg 1$, using this norm incurs a penalty like $ |k \delta(\Lambda)|^{1/2}$ when used to control $L^\infty$. Nevertheless, this loss can be compensated by taking sufficiently regular data. This is one of the main reasons for the difference in $k$ dependence between Theorem \ref{thm2} and \cite[Theorem~1.2]{CJWZ25}.

title: Remark
body_md: Note that logarithmic singularities of the form $c(y)\cdot\log((b(y)-\lambda+i\iota\epsilon))^{\alpha}$ are not uniformly in $L^2$ as $\epsilon\to0$ if $c(y)$ is merely in $L^2$. This is the reason why the source term $c_{3}(y)\log(b(y)-\lambda+i\iota\epsilon)$ is singled out in \eqref{ndrayf}. As shown in the proof, the source term\\ $c_{3}(y)\log(b(y)-\lambda+i\iota\epsilon)$ plays a role that is almost the same as the source term $c_4(y)$. However, by taking the logarithmic source term out of the general term, we get to track the lowest regularity required for the coefficient functions. This is also the reason why $p=2$ is not achievable in \eqref{ndraygeneral2}. When taking higher derivatives of $f$, the $\delta$ term from the second $y$-derivative of the Green's function produces singularities such as $c_1'(y)\log^2(b(y)-\lambda+i\iota\epsilon)$, as shown in \eqref{ndraygeneral4}. Under the stated regularity assumptions on the coefficients, these need not belong to $L^2$. Lemma \ref{ndraygeneral} is particularly useful in estimating the highest derivatives of the spectral density function.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:bdds}
Let $\lambda \in \Sigma_{j,\delta_0} \setminus \{b(y_{j*})\},  \epsilon \in (0, \epsilon_0), \theta \in (0, 1/4]$, $\iota\in \{-, +\}$, and  $ \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(y,\lambda)$ be defined as in \eqref{eq:Erhs}. Then   the following bounds hold for $\alpha \in \{0,1\}$ and $|k \delta(\Lambda)| \ll 1$ with a constant depending on $\theta$.
               
                                                                                                                                 
             
\begin{subequations}
    \begin{align}
   |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) dz |&\lesssim   
   \frac{ \norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}   \varrho_{j,k}^2(y; \Lambda)}{|k|^{3/2 - \theta}}, \\
                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                   
   |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda)\partial_\lambda \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) dz |  &\lesssim \frac{ \norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}   }{|k|^{3/2 - \theta}  }, \\
  |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) {D_\lambda} \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) dz| &\lesssim \frac{\norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}  \varrho_{j, k}(y; \Lambda) }{|k|^{3/2 -\theta}},   \\
   |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) \partial_\lambda^2 \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) dz| &\lesssim    \frac{ \norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}   }{|k|^{3/2- \theta } \delta(\Lambda) {\varrho_j}(y; \Lambda)},  \\ 
   |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda)\partial_\lambda {D_\lambda} \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) dz| &\lesssim \frac{\norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}  }{|k|^{3/2 - \theta } \delta(\Lambda)},  \\
    |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda)\partial_\lambda^3 \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) dz|  &\lesssim    \frac{ \norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}   }{|k|^{3/2 - \theta} \delta^3(\Lambda) \varrho_{j}(y; \Lambda)  },  \\
    |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) \partial_\lambda^2 {D_\lambda} \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) dz| &\lesssim \frac{\norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}  }{|k|^{3/2 - \theta} \delta^3(\Lambda) }, \\
    |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) D_\lambda^2 ( \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) - {g^\iota_{k,\epsilon}(z,\lambda)}) dz|  &\lesssim \frac{\norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}  {\varrho_{j,k}}(y; \Lambda)  }{|k|^{3/2-\theta}\delta(\Lambda)}, \\
      |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) \partial_\lambda D_\lambda^2 ( \mathcal{R}_{0, 0, \epsilon}^\iota(z - y_{j*},\lambda) - {g^\iota_{k,\epsilon}(z,\lambda)}) dz|  &\lesssim \frac{\norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}  {\varrho_{j,k}}(y; \Lambda)  }{|k|^{3/2-\theta}\delta^3(\Lambda)}, \\
     |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) D_\lambda^2 {g^\iota_{k,\epsilon}(z,\lambda)} dz|  &\lesssim \frac{\norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}}{|k|^{3/2}},\\
     |\int_\mathbb{T} {\varrho_{j,k}^\alpha}(y; \Lambda)  \partial_y^\alpha  \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) \partial_\lambda D_\lambda^2 {g^\iota_{k,\epsilon}(z,\lambda)} dz|  &\lesssim \frac{\norm{\omega_{0k}}_{H_k^4}}{|k|^{3/2}}.
\end{align}
\end{subequations}

title: Proof
body_md:
Equations \eqref{BDC2}, \eqref{E:eq}, and \eqref{rhs:F} yield
\begin{align}
&\left(
-\partial_y^2+k^2
+\frac{b''(y)}{b(y)-\lambda+i\iota \epsilon}
\right) \partial_\lambda D_\lambda \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota(y,\lambda)
\\
&\quad = -2b''(y)\partial_y\partial_\lambda^2 \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota(y,\lambda )
  -b'''(y)\partial_\lambda^2 \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota(y,\lambda )
  -\frac{b'''(y)}{b(y)-\lambda+i \iota \epsilon}\partial_\lambda \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota(y,\lambda )\notag \\
&\quad-\frac{b''(y)}{\bigl(b(y)-\lambda+i \iota \epsilon\bigr)^2}D_\lambda \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota(y,\lambda )
  -\frac{b'''(y)}{\bigl(b(y)-\lambda+i\iota \epsilon\bigr)^2}\digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota(y,\lambda )  +  D_\lambda\partial_\lambda r. \notag
\end{align}
Denoting the right-hand side of the equation satisfied by $\partial_\lambda  D_\lambda \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota(y,\lambda) - \mathcal{S}_{1,1, \epsilon}^\iota $ as $\mathcal{R}_{1,1, \epsilon}^\iota$, we solve for $\partial_\lambda D_\lambda \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota   -  \mathcal{S}_{1,1, \epsilon}^\iota$ as follows:
\begin{align}
    \partial_\lambda D_\lambda \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota   -  \mathcal{S}_{1,1, \epsilon}^\iota   + T_\Theta (\partial_\lambda D_\lambda \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota   -  \mathcal{S}_{1,1, \epsilon}^\iota) = \int_\mathbb{T} \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) \mathcal{R}_{1,1,\epsilon}^\iota(z,\lambda) dz .
\end{align}
After a direct computation to determine $\mathcal{R}_{1,1, \epsilon}^\iota$,
\eqref{DCM5} follows from  Proposition \ref{DeC7}, the estimates \eqref{DCM2}, \eqref{DCM9.4}, and Lemmas \ref{dint}, \ref{g:bdds}, \ref{gr:bdds}, and \ref{mGk50}.

label: rem:lamgd
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:lamgd}
    The reason for the separate cases in \eqref{gDCM22} is related to how smallness manifests in the modified Green's function in the different cases. When $|k \delta(\Lambda)| \ll 1$, the modified Green's function only enforces localized smallness near the critical point which is why we use $X^{0, -1}$ and a $\delta(\Lambda)$ weight. However, when $|k \delta(\Lambda)| \gtrsim 1$, the modified Green's function is small everywhere. This can compensate for the global $\delta(\Lambda)$ factor on the right hand side of the equation and allows the use of $X^{0,0}$.

label: gd2F
title: Proof
body_md:
Equations \eqref{BDC2}, \eqref{E:eq}, and \eqref{rhs:F} yield
\begin{align}
\label{gd2F}
&\left(-\partial_y^2 + k^2 + \frac{b''(y)}{b(y) - \lambda + i \iota \epsilon } \right) D_\lambda^2 \digamma^\iota (y,\lambda)\\
    &= -4b''(y)\partial_y\partial_\lambdaD_\lambda \digamma^\iota (y,\lambda)
  -2b'''(y)\partial_\lambda D_\lambda \digamma^\iota (y,\lambda)
  +2\bigl(b''(y)\bigr)^2\partial_\lambda^2 \digamma^\iota (y,\lambda) \notag\\
&-2b'''(y)\partial_y\partial_\lambda \digamma^\iota (y,\lambda)-b''''(y)\partial_\lambda \digamma^\iota (y,\lambda)
  -\frac{2b'''(y)}{b(y)-\lambda+i \iota \epsilon}D_\lambda \digamma^\iota (y,\lambda)
  -\frac{b''''(y)}{b(y)-\lambda+i\iota \epsilon}\digamma^\iota (y,\lambda)\notag \\
  &+ D_\lambda^2 r. \notag
\end{align}
Denoting the right-hand side  of \eqref{gd2F} as $\mathcal{R}_{0,2, \epsilon}^\iota$, we solve for $D_\lambda^2 \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota$ as follows:
\begin{align}
  D_\lambda^2 \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota   + T_\Theta (D_\lambda^2 \digamma_{k, \epsilon}^\iota) = \int_\mathbb{T} \mathcal{G}_k^j(y,z; \Lambda) \mathcal{R}_{0,2, \epsilon}^\iota(z,\lambda) dz .
\end{align}
The bound \eqref{gDCM22} follows from  Proposition \ref{DeC7}, and  Lemmas  \ref{lem:lam1} , \ref{lem:gd2}, \ref{dint}, \ref{g:bdds}, \ref{gr:bdds}, and \ref{mGk50}.
